PDF p.8 = journal p.779, Secs. 4.1.3-4.3: unit-information prior giving O(n^-1/2), n as Hessian growth rate, pr1 simple Monte Carlo, (10) self-normalized importance ratio with w=pi/pi*, (11) harmonic mean converging a.s. without a general Gaussian CLT

components.note: Definition states measurable Theta_n containing a fixed ball, h_n valued in R or -infinity, finite nonnegative measurable a_n, C^4/C^2 regularity on the ball, zero gradient, eigenvalues of J_n in [c,C], uniform bound A on D^3h, D^4h, Da, D^2a, a_- <= a_n(theta_n) <= a_+, local quadratic domination c_0, exponential outside-tail bound A_T e^{-eta n}, and fixes the norms and Lebesgue measure. Worked boundaries where the interior-ball, one-mode tail and positive-curvature premises fail are computed in the normal-example theorem and its annex proof.

Statement gives the explicit approximant, relative error 1+O(n^-1) with a uniform constant, positivity and finiteness, and the factor and log-factor assertions. The annex proof writes positivity/finiteness, the rescaling u=sqrt(n)(theta-theta_n) with b_n=n^{1/12}, Taylor expansions with explicit remainders, odd-term cancellation, Gaussian tail moments, the Gaussian integral by Schur-complement induction, the middle and outside region bounds, the lower bound on the main term, and the two-model factor/log steps. Consistent with source p.778 (relative error O(n^-1) under stated conditions).

Posterior-mode (source (4)) and MLE (source (5), p.778) constructions are both stated with separate hypothesis checks; the annex proof writes the exponent/amplitude choices and the determinant identity. The source remark that (5) is likely less accurate when the prior is informative relative to the likelihood (p.778) is preserved at body lines 116-119.

Lemma states symmetric J_n with eigenvalues >= c, ||J~_n-J_n|| <= delta_n < c/2, the bound d delta_n/c and the O(n^-1/2)/O(n^-1) consequences, and that the name expected information does not supply the bound. The annex writes the normalized matrix E, its eigenvalue bound, the determinant product and the |log(1+t)| <= 2|t| step. The source's expected-information variant with error O(n^-1/2) (p.778) is preserved and attained exactly by the logistic boundary theorem (body 139-181, annex 346-427), which also gives a data sequence where the comparison fails.

Theorem defines c_{k,n}, proves c_{k,n}=O(1), the log-evidence expansion, the BIC relation retaining the c-terms, the parameter-free case, the O(1) error from discarding the c-terms, the ratio limit e^{-c_*}, and restricts the source's relative statement (9) to |log B_10| -> infinity. The full two-model display with coefficient two on both prior-log terms and n as the information-growth rate (source p.779) follow. The annex writes each step. The source's unit-information O(n^-1/2) Schwarz variant (p.779) is stated with explicit premises and proved (annex 492-559), with a normal instance showing that the local-alternative premise cannot be dropped.

Exact normal calculation: posterior-Laplace exactness, the explicit MLE ratio, verification of the hypotheses for bounded x_n, the four point-null factors and the BIC-to-exact ratio two. Three failure boundaries (boundary mode, two modes, quartic zero curvature) with Bernoulli realizations under proper priors. The annex computes each value and verifies each premise and its failure.

Unbiasedness, almost-sure convergence under integrability alone (Etemadi strong law, strong-laws-of-large-numbers.tex line 133) and the variance under a finite second moment; proof written. Source simple Monte Carlo estimate pr1 (p.779) preserved.

Ordinary importance (T << Q, finite version V, unbiased, almost-sure limit, variance) and source equation (10) in self-normalized form (Pi << Q, eventually defined, consistent, not necessarily unbiased, density form W=pi/q with support domination) are stated and proved. Finite-sample bias and support failures are calculated in C011 items 1-2. The identification of (10) as the self-normalized ratio was checked against source p.779.

Reciprocal identities E_P H=1/I and its second moment, unbiasedness of A_M and the non-unbiasedness of its inverse, almost-sure convergence, the classical case with Pi << T iff L>0 Pi-a.e. (both directions written), the variance condition on int L^{-1} dPi, the wrong limit I/s when Pi(L>0)=s<1, and the generalized density form (12) with its support and second-moment requirement; proof steps written. Source (11)/(12) (pp.779-780) preserved.

Normal limits for the ordinary mean, self-normalized importance (v_SN) and the generalized harmonic mean (I^4 v_H), with the zero-variance convention and zero-denominator defaults. The proof uses thm:p15-clt-iid and thm:p15-clt-perturbation (central-limit-theorems.tex lines 76 and 90) and writes the numerator/denominator and inverse identities. The explicit refusal of a normal limit without the moment premises preserves the source's statement that (11) does not generally satisfy a Gaussian CLT (p.779).

Five calculated examples: support failure (direct relative variance, zero probability, harmonic estimate one, zero-variance ordinary importance versus self-normalized one), bias (importance variance 16/3, self-normalized expectation 3/2, harmonic expectation 5/2 with unbiased reciprocal 1/2, realizable likelihood values), infinite importance variance, harmonic reciprocal variance infinite iff tau^2 >= s^2 with a finite first moment, and the stationary identity-chain dependence failure. Every value is computed in the annex.
